newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps all firm, bar reluctant fuel.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps all firm, bar reluctant fuel.

text.p: European oil swaps were steady to firmer on Tuesday as crude futures strengthened, traders said.
Brent crude CFDs were a few cents stronger, gasoline was $2-3 firmer taking a cue from the NYMEX contract, while naphtha edged up $1.
Dealers a fair degree of swaps activity had been restricted to spread trading and that the market remained in the summer doldrums.
Brent CFDs saw the balance of this week firm to -16/17 cents against September from -18 cents while July 21-25 showed a more significant gain to -18 cents from -22/23 cents from September.
Further out the gain was restricted to a couple of cents with July 28-August 1 talked around -23 cents against September and August 4-8 assessed at -24 cents.

Gasoline showed some strength as NYMEX gasoline went higher and tight physical supply continued. A 10,000 tonne parcel was rumoured done at $186.50 fob and eurograde barges were done at $184.00 fob ARA, $184.50 fob AR, $185.00 fob AR and $186.50 for Rotterdam running refinery material.
July was not yet dead although most players were looking for indications for spread trading purposes. August/September was done at a p+c level.

Fuel was lacklustre again and showing signs it was not ready to follow the energy complex to every twist and turn in the market. With Singapore levels showing renweded signs of weakness the European market could fall in the next couple of days, traders said.
"Spreads and east/west is talking," said one.
July was talked at $86-87 with August valued around $87.25 and 4Q traded at $92.50.
Rolling July into August, which started in earnest on Monday, continued today, dealers said.
Naphtha was about $1 firmer, taking comfort from higher gasoline and crude levels, but there was little business thought done. August was pegged at $181-182.
